visual_review: All four corrected full-body outputs inspected. Each hand has four individual fingers and an opposable thumb. White backdrop, full silhouette and simple angular geometry retained.

concepts.alt: Charcoal and orange PS1-style stag beetle mech with split-shell shoulders, two blunt head prongs, and five separate blocky digits on each hand
concepts.review: The broad split-shell shoulders, blunt sensor prongs and planted stance establish a heavy beetle silhouette. Broad flat armor faces remain readable. Both hands show four separate fingers and a side thumb after correction.
concepts.initial_review: Agent rejected for hand count: the hand on the right side of the image had three fingers plus a thumb.

concepts.alt: Tall olive and bone-gray low-poly mantis mech with raised wedge shoulders, long limbs, and five separate blocky digits on each hand
concepts.review: The tall narrow torso, triangular head and raised shoulder wedges make this the lightest insect-inspired direction. Long forearm shells preserve the folded-mantis idea while leaving ordinary manipulators usable. Both hands show four fingers and a thumb.
concepts.initial_review: Agent rejected for hand count: both hands had only three fingers plus a thumb.

concepts.alt: Blue-black low-poly raven mech with a wedge sensor beak, swept triangular shoulder armor, and five separate blocky digits on each hand
concepts.review: The swept shoulder planes and forward sensor wedge carry the bird influence clearly. Both hands show four fingers and a thumb. The legs read straighter than the proposed reverse-joint frame; a stronger hock silhouette is a possible refinement.

concepts.alt: Sand and rust-red low-poly hound mech with a forward wedge head, tapered waist, long runner legs, and five separate blocky digits on each hand
concepts.review: The low wedge head, paired sensor fins and tucked waist suggest a pursuit frame. Its animal cue is subtler than the beetle or raven. Both hands show four fingers and a thumb; armor and body pose remain consistent with the initial take.
